verified_signals.signal: FLEET BASELINE NOW SETTLED AND MACHINE-COUNTED. Counted in Python: 112 'Filijala' (branches), 457 'Bankomat' (plain cash-out ATM), 111 'Multifunkcionalni bankomat' (multifunctional/deposit-capable ATM) and 59 'ATS' units (unattended self-service cash-deposit/vault stations, most tagged 0-24h at branch addresses). verified_signals.source_name: AikBank - public branch/ATM locator data file (maps-formated.json), corroborated by the audited FY2025 financial statements incl. Annual Business Report 2025

verified_signals.signal: HARD REGULATORY DEADLINE FOR eKYC, WITH A NEW UNATTENDED-IDENTIFICATION ROUTE. TRANSITION DEADLINES: institutions already running video identification must align their business and internal acts within SIX MONTHS of entry into force, and adapt their TECHNICAL SOLUTIONS within TWELVE MONTHS.

verified_signals.signal: SECTOR CONTEXT FROM AIKBANK'S OWN REPORT. In November 2025 the Serbian banking sector had 19 banks, 78.1% foreign-owned by share, operating through 1,289 BRANCHES, with 48 branches having ceased operations during 2025 and total sector employment of 21,786 - itself down by 500 over the year. Sector assets were EUR 58,483m in Q3-2025 (+8.5% year on year), pre-tax profit for the first nine months EUR 1,220.8m (+1.2%), average ROE 20.6% in September 2025. Against that, AikBank's 112 branches are about 8.7% of the country's branch network while its 568 ATMs are 17.0% of the national ATM park - it is roughly twice as self-service-weighted as the average Serbian bank.
verified_signals.source_name: AikBank - Annual Business Report 2025, 'Bankarski sektor' section (inside the audited FY2025 PDF); ATM share computed against NBS acceptance-network statistics
verified_signals.implies: An ATM-heavy, branch-light profile in a market that closed 48 branches and shed 500 banking jobs in a single year means AikBank's channel strategy runs through machines. That is the structural reason its self-service spend should outgrow peers, and the number to lead a pitch with.
verified_signals.likelihood: Branch consolidation continuing sector-wide
verified_signals.followup: Benchmark AikBank's ATMs-per-branch ratio (about 5.1) against Banca Intesa, OTP and NLB Komercijalna when pitching; those units are covered by other agents this run.

The 1,289 branches and the 48 that ceased operating ARE confirmed verbatim, as is the November-2025 reference period (which the researcher presented as 'end-2025'). I also pulled the surrounding sector figures the researcher dropped (19 banks, 78.1% foreign-owned, EUR 58,483m assets, EUR 1,220.8m 9M profit, 20.6% ROE) and recomputed AikBank's shares off the verified counts: 112/1,289 = 8.7% of branches and 568/3,336 = 17.0% of ATMs, versus the researcher's '9%' and '~15%'. residual_gaps:

No browser session was needed. Recommend this endpoint be snapshotted monthly.

STILL OPEN. (1) The 75-unit Printec/NCR Atleos deployment at AikBank remains unverifiable outside Printec - printecgroup.com's own site search for 'AIK' returns nothing, and the figure appears only in LinkedIn-derived summaries. It must be confirmed internally or dropped. (2) AikBank's ATM OEM mix is nowhere disclosed; the FY2025 report never names a hardware vendor, and the locator carries no vendor field. (3) What 'ATS' actually denotes in AikBank's locator (59 units, mostly 0-24h at branch addresses, plausibly automated deposit/vault stations) is my inference from context and needs confirming with the bank. (4) The bank contradicts itself on Hipotekarna banka's Montenegrin ATM count: 47 in the 30/06/2026 news item, 56 on the /stanovnistvo/zona-24-7/ page on 31/07/2026; neither Gorenjska's 66 nor Hipotekarna's number was verified against those banks' own locators, which is the obvious next step. (5) AikBank's POS terminal count and vendor mix are not published. (6) Whether 'Multifunkcionalni bankomat' means true cash recycling (re-dispensing deposited notes) or deposit-plus-dispense on separate cassettes is not stated - recycler-class is an inference from published function, and Printec should not assert it to the customer. (7) The 12-month eKYC technical-compliance deadline cannot be pinned to a calendar date until the Gazette 43/2026 publication date is confirmed from the Official Gazette itself.

ACCESS ISSUES LOGGED. (a) aikbank.rs serves its PDFs gzip-encoded with a .pdf extension - pdfminer fails with 'No /Root object' until the file is gunzipped; this bit both the FY2025 report and the H1-2026 statements. (b) zse.hr/hr/papir/310 returns HTTP 200 but is an Angular app that renders no disclosure list to a plain fetch, and zse.hr/api/... paths 404 - the previous run's ZSE citation is therefore unreadable by anyone following it, and I substituted Podravska banka's own investor-notices page, which carries the same disclosure sequence. (c) The SEC EX-99.1 copy of the Brink's/Atleos release returns 403 to the fetch tool; the identical GlobeNewswire copy was readable and was used to verify terms. (d) printecgroup.com returns 403 to the fetch tool but 200 to a desktop-User-Agent curl; its own search page threw a WordPress 500 on one query. (e) Podravska banka's takeover-obligation PDF is a scanned image with no extractable text, so the precise per-share price could not be verified from the primary document and was rounded to ~EUR 68.8 from Croatian press. (f) NBS statistics: the legacy .xls files are BIFF and unreadable with openpyxl, but the parallel .xlsx files under /statistika/el_novac/ carry the same series and were used. (g) Podravska banka's ENGLISH network page is stale relative to the Croatian one (it still lists a Krizevci branch) - always read poba.hr in Croatian.
